summary: Afternoon sustained 5xx gradient after ephemeral-worker rebalance and upstream runtime OOMs
description:
Issue summary:
During the 14:00–15:10 UTC window on 2026-03-13 we observed a stepped increase in 5xx responses from the API Gateway for a subset of requests routed to dedicated pools serving AceroHealth. The increase coincided with an ephemeral-worker rebalance triggered by autoscaler activity and several upstream serving-runtime processes reporting OOMs and graceful shutdowns.

Impact:
- Customer requests returning 502/503/504; visible degradation across both sync generation and streaming endpoints.
- Customer-reported error rate ~18% peak (baseline ~0.6%).
- Some long-lived streaming sessions disconnected without retries succeeding.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east) dedicated pool for AceroHealth (tenant id: ac-7641).
- Autoscaler policy: aggressive scale-in with 5m cooldown.
- Model: gptx-1-large-v2 pinned by customer.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Autoscaler triggers scale-in due to aggregate metric dip at 13:56 UTC.
2) Ephemeral worker rebalance moves several sessions and drains connections from older proxies (14:02 UTC).
3) Serving-runtime observed KV cache eviction pressure and increased GPU memory allocation churn.
4) At 14:05–14:08 UTC multiple runtime workers hit GPU memory fragmentation thresholds and OOM, restarting.
5) API Gateway request fanout to upstreams encounters half-open connections, resulting in 502/503 and some 504 timeouts.

Relevant logs / excerpts:
[apigw] 2026-03-13T14:06:12Z WARN upstream reset for tenant ac-7641 route /v1/generate 502 conn-reset
[runtime] 2026-03-13T14:07:01Z ERROR gpu_allocator OOM while serving request shard=3 model=gptx-1-large-v2 pid=2245
[autoscaler] 2026-03-13T13:58:40Z INFO scale-in initiated from 12->8 replicas (cooldown enforced)

Initial mitigation applied:
- Support routed traffic away from affected dedicated pool to a warmed standby pool (14:12 UTC) which reduced 5xx rate to ~2.2%.
- Disabled aggressive scale-in policy for the pool (toggled to conservative) to prevent immediate reseed.
- Temporarily disabled prefetch eviction on the runtime for this tenant to reduce KV churn.

Current hypothesis:
- Aggressive scale-in caused ephemeral worker rebalance that exacerbated GPU memory fragmentation on a subset of workers; fragmentation led to OOM restarts which made upstreams intermittently unhealthy. API Gateway observed half-open connections and increased retry/backoff which amplified 5xx rates.

Next steps:
- SRE to collect full runtime nvml logs and heap/KV cache eviction traces (run: /opt/infra/bin/collect-runtime-traces --tenant ac-7641).
- Engineering to review GPU allocator changes in PR referenced below for potential regressions.
- Work with product to provide customers an advisory about pinning warm pool sizes or adjusting autoscaler cooldowns until fix is deployed.
comments: 2026-03-13 14:18 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer-facing report: AceroHealth reported increased 502s and disconnects starting ~14:00 UTC. Provided initial acknowledgment and moved to P1 escalation.

2026-03-13 14:25 UTC - Marcus Liang (Oncall SRE): Observed correlated spikes in runtime OOMs and autoscaler scale-in events. Redirected traffic to standby pool; error rate dropped but not to baseline. Collecting runtime logs and nvml traces.

2026-03-13 14:40 UTC - Marcus Liang (Oncall SRE): Found pattern of worker restart loops after prefetch eviction storms. Suspect fragmentation + allocator path causing OOM under drain conditions. Linked PR for allocator experiments: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3472.

2026-03-13 15:05 UTC - Engineering (runtime): Reproduced memory fragmentation locally with synthetic drain test. Confirmed allocator returns could be improved; preparing patch to reduce transient allocations during connection drain.

2026-03-13 15:25 UTC - Support (Aisha Patel): Notified AceroHealth of mitigation steps (traffic reroute, autoscaler policy change). Customer reports partial restoration; they will monitor and escalate if errors reoccur.

2026-03-14 09:10 UTC - Marcus Liang: Follow-up: patch candidate posted, running canary against a small dedicated pool during low traffic to validate reduction in OOM restarts. Added follow-up action to update runbook for aggressive scale-in detection.

2026-03-14 12:00 UTC - Engineering (runtime): Canary results show stable memory metrics and no OOMs over 2h. Plan: schedule rolling hotfix to serving-runtime in next maintenance window (2026-03-15 01:00 UTC).
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigations: traffic reroute to standby pool, disabled aggressive scale-in, turned off prefetch eviction for tenant. Long-term: runtime allocator patch to reduce fragmentation during drain and autoscaler tuning; update runbook to detect rebalance-induced OOM patterns. Hotfix scheduled and PR under review.
